ai.description: *Bunopus orientalis* reaches 10 cm. It is sandy-brown with dark dorsal crossbars. Distinctive features include a slender, tuberculate body and a tail longer than the snout-vent length.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Bunopus orientalis* is best distinguished by its lack of enlarged tubercles on the back, which are present in most other regional geckos, giving it a smooth appearance.
ai.habitat: The Sind gecko inhabits arid, sandy desert regions and scrublands in the Indian subcontinent, typically at low elevations, often sheltering under rocks or in burrows.
ai.behavior: The Sind gecko is strictly nocturnal, emerging after sunset to forage for small insects and spiders across the sandy desert dunes of its arid habitat.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Bunopus orientalis* is oviparous, typically laying a clutch of two eggs. Breeding occurs during the warmer months, generally between April and June.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Bunopus orientalis* is found in the arid regions of Pakistan’s Sindh and Balochistan provinces, typically inhabiting sandy or gravelly desert lowlands.
